profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the engineering platform team and the internal research enablement team at a mid-sized developer tools company. The company is preparing an internal knowledge brief and searchable evidence page on 'Psychological safety in software workplaces' based on a newly completed systematic literature review. The platform team is responsible for integrating the review content into the engineering knowledge portal, while the research enablement team is responsible for delivering the synthesized artifacts and metadata. The meeting context is that both teams need to align on the handoff for the review package before Friday so the portal update can go live ahead of the quarterly engineering managers' summit. The agenda is to confirm what will be delivered, what 'final' means for the handoff, which version of the review data will be used, and who will update the shared evidence taxonomy file in the repository. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the Friday handoff, portal integration steps, and ownership of the shared artifacts.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Internal developer portals, content schemas, documentation pipelines, release coordination
members.background: Nina leads the team that maintains the company's engineering knowledge portal and its nightly content ingestion pipeline; she previously worked as a backend engineer on documentation infrastructure and now coordinates cross-team content launches.
members.private_state: Nina wants a smooth portal update with minimal manual cleanup because her team is already overloaded with a search index migration; she is trying to avoid last-minute schema changes or ownership ambiguity that would create operational work after the handoff.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final package' means portal-ready assets that conform to the existing ingestion schema and require no further restructuring by her team.
The 'coded dataset' refers to the frozen CSV export already used in staging last week, not an actively edited analysis workbook.
If a shared taxonomy file sits in the platform repository, the content-producing team updates it as part of their handoff rather than asking platform to make semantic edits.
When someone says the content is 'ready for Friday,' that means it has already passed the standard portal validation checks and can be merged during the Friday release window.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Evidence synthesis, qualitative coding, literature review workflows, internal research reporting
members.background: Leo supports internal evidence reviews for engineering leadership and recently coordinated the systematic literature review on psychological safety in software engineering, including article screening, coding, and synthesis with a small research operations group.
members.private_state: Leo wants to preserve flexibility to make minor synthesis edits until late in the week because the review team is still normalizing some coded categories; he also wants the platform team to absorb repository-specific adjustments since his team does not usually work inside the portal codebase.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final package' means the substantive findings and narrative are complete, even if column names, file layout, or metadata tags still need light adaptation for the portal.
The 'coded dataset' refers to the master Airtable export that remains the source of truth until publication, even if earlier CSV snapshots exist.
Ownership of the shared taxonomy file belongs to the platform team because it lives in their repo and affects portal behavior beyond this one review.
When someone says the content is 'ready for Friday,' that means the research conclusions are stable enough to hand over by end of day, with operational validation happening afterward if needed.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the final package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree Leo will send the 'final package' on Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the final package will be fully portal-ready: schema-compliant JSON/CSV, approved summary text, stable taxonomy tags, and no additional formatting work needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the final package will contain the completed review findings and supporting files, but the platform team may still need to adapt naming, structure, or metadata to fit portal requirements.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-team coordination, 'final package' sounds like a routine handoff term, and both assume the other shares their normal workflow conventions, so neither feels a need to unpack the acceptance standard.

misalignment_points.topic: Which coded dataset is the source for integration
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using 'the coded dataset' for the evidence page.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the frozen CSV snapshot named ps_slr_codes_v3.csv that was uploaded to the staging folder and tested against the ingestion pipeline last Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the current Airtable-derived master export, which may become ps_slr_codes_v4.csv after late recoding of antecedent and consequence categories.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have been discussing the same review for days, so 'the coded dataset' feels uniquely identifiable; the differing concrete file instances remain invisible because each assumes there is one obvious current version.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership of the shared taxonomy file
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the taxonomy file will be 'updated for the PS review.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Leo's team will edit the content-level taxonomy entries for antecedents, consequences, and study context labels, because those semantic additions are part of the review deliverable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes his team will provide a list of recommended tags, while M1's team will make the actual changes in the taxonomy YAML since the file is part of the platform repository and linked to other portal collections.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'update the taxonomy file' compresses several sub-tasks—proposing labels, editing YAML, validating dependencies, and merging—so each person silently includes different boundaries while hearing the same coordination statement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the review should be 'ready for Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means ready before the Friday 2 p.m. release cutoff, with validation already passed so her team can merge and publish in that day's release.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means delivered by Friday end of day as the completed research handoff, with any repository checks or portal validation able to happen afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline shorthand like 'ready for Friday' is common and usually sufficient in ordinary conversation; because both are cooperative and talking about the same target week, the phrase creates a strong illusion of precise alignment.

turns.inner_thought: I need to lock this down now. My team is already underwater with the search index migration, so I cannot absorb surprise cleanup on Friday. If this is going into the Friday release, I need it actually ready before the 2 p.m. cutoff, validated, and conforming to the existing ingestion schema. Hopefully Leo is just confirming a normal handoff and not leaving edge cases for us.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I want to make sure we have a clean path to get the psychological safety review into the portal ahead of the managers' summit. From your side, is everything still on track to be ready for Friday?

turns.inner_thought: The findings are basically settled, which is the important part. We still have a little normalization work on some coding categories, but that's routine and shouldn't affect the overall story. I can send the final package Friday once the team has done one more pass; platform can handle any repo-specific fit and finish after that.
turns.utterance: Yes, we’re in good shape. The synthesis on antecedents and consequences has stabilized, and I’m planning to send the final package on Friday. So from the review side, it should be ready for Friday.

turns.utterance: Great. On our side, we can wire the evidence page pretty quickly as long as the coded dataset is the same one we already exercised in staging. Should we just continue from the coded dataset?

turns.inner_thought: Yes, we’ll use the coded dataset—the current master export is still the source of truth. I am still cleaning up a few category labels in Airtable, and it may end up as the next export version by the time I send it over, but that’s just normal refinement and shouldn’t matter from their perspective.
turns.utterance: Yes, let’s use the coded dataset. I’m just cleaning up a few category labels from the master sheet before handoff, but that shouldn’t change the plan for the evidence page.

turns.inner_thought: If the final package is truly final, the portal job should ingest the summary, study table, and tags without my team having to restructure anything. I need this to be a drop-in handoff, not another Friday afternoon formatting exercise.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. Once the final package lands, the portal job should be able to ingest the summary, study table, and tags without much extra work on our side.

turns.inner_thought: I can definitely provide the completed findings bundle: narrative, evidence table export, and the labels we’ve been using. But I’m not planning to reshape files around their portal conventions ourselves; that kind of adaptation sits with platform since they own the repo and ingestion setup.
turns.utterance: Right, I’ll include the narrative summary, the evidence table export, and the recommended labels. Any portal-specific reshaping can happen during integration.

turns.inner_thought: I need their team to actually make the semantic additions for this review. The taxonomy file lives in our repo, sure, but the content-level entries for antecedents, consequences, and context labels should come from the content owners and be part of the handoff. I don’t have capacity for semantic editing right now.
turns.utterance: The other thing I wanted to check is the shared taxonomy file. It just needs to be updated for the PS review so the new antecedent and consequence facets show up correctly.

turns.inner_thought: That’s fine—we already have the labels the research group has been using. I’ll send those over, and Nina’s team can put them into the taxonomy YAML since they manage the repository and know what else the file touches.
turns.utterance: Yes, absolutely. I’ll send over the taxonomy additions my team has been using so your side can drop them into the repo.

turns.inner_thought: I should make the timing explicit without getting dragged into details. We need the handoff before the Friday release window, not by end of day, and ideally it has already passed standard validation so we can merge. If he says 'ready for Friday' the normal cross-team meaning should cover that.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Just as a timing note, we usually need the handoff before the Friday release window so we can run validation and merge the content the same day.

turns.inner_thought: That should still be manageable. The review will be ready Friday, and I only expect minor touch-ups to the coding export before I send it. If their validation runs after we hand it over, that’s part of their process; the substantive work should be complete on our side by then.
turns.utterance: That should be fine. The review will be ready for Friday, and I’m only expecting minor touch-ups to the coded dataset before I send it.

turns.inner_thought: Okay, then I can prep the page shell and assume I’m getting a portal-ready final package plus the taxonomy update on Friday. If that lands cleanly, we can close this without adding more work to my team.
turns.utterance: Great. I’ll have my team prepare the page shell, and I’ll expect the final package plus the taxonomy update to arrive Friday so we can close the loop.

turns.inner_thought: That lines up. I’ll send the completed review materials once the last pass is done—the final package, the coded dataset, and the taxonomy additions—and then platform can take it through the repo steps.
